name: Ceredig Wledig

attributes.attribute: possibly the Coroticus of St Patrick's writings

text: Ceredig Wledig was a sixth-century ruler of Dumbarton, within the kingdom of Strathclyde in Scotland. His Welsh title Gwledig may mean kind, or else rustic and rural in a second sense. He is possibly the Coroticus of St Patrick's writings, who kidnapped some of the saint's earliest converts to Christianity.

okr.objective: Ceredig Wledig is a sixth-century ruler of Dumbarton who may be the Coroticus of St Patrick's writings.
key_results: Ceredig Wledig ruled Dumbarton in the kingdom of Strathclyde, Scotland, in the sixth century.
Gwledig is a Welsh term for kind or, secondly, rustic or rural.
He is possibly the Coroticus who kidnapped St Patrick's early converts to Christianity.
